newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-CHRONOLOGY OF GRAF TAX INVESTIGATION AND TRIAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHRONOLOGY OF GRAF TAX INVESTIGATION AND TRIAL.

text.p: Here is a brief chronology of the tax investigation and trial of Steffi Graf's father Peter which ended on Friday, including Graf's remarkable performances on court during the period.
1994 - German tax authorities fear that not all of Steffi Graf's earnings are being declared.
March 1995 - Authorities ask Graf adviser Joachim Eckardt for details of undeclared earnings by April 21. None are given.
April 26 1995 - Official start of tax investigations.
May 23 1995 - Tax authorities search Graf homes in Germany.
June 10 1995 - Steffi wins French Open tennis championships.
July 8 1995 - Steffi wins Wimbledon.
July 12 1995 - German media break news of May tax raids, the start of intense media coverage during the scandal.
August 2 1995 - Peter Graf arrested, refused bail and jailed while investigation continues because authorities fear he might leave the country. Receives hospital treatment.
September 9 1995 - Steffi wins U.S. Open but leaves press conference in tears after being asked about father.
September 26 1995 - Eckardt also arrested and put in jail. In the next few months courts refuse several times to release the two men on bail.
October 1995 - German car firm Opel end 10-year sponsorship deal with Steffi, one of the longest in German sport.
April 17 1996 - Peter Graf and Eckardt, still in prison, are accused of avoiding around $11.5 million in tax.
June 8 1996 - Steffi wins fifth French Open title.
July 6 1996 - Steffi wins seventh Wimbledon singles title.
September 5 1996 - Court case starts in Mannheim.
September 8 1996 - Steffi wins fifth U.S. Open title
November 15 1996 - Peter Graf released from jail after paying $3.3 million in bail after 15 months in custody. Steffi, playing in U.S., says she can't wait to get home to see him.
Jan 14 1997 - German prosecutors ask court to jail Peter Graf for six years and nine months.
Jan 15 1997 - Women's tennis tour organisers (WTA) say they probing allegations Steffi took appearance money for tournaments which is banned.
Jan 19 1997 - Steffi's campaign for fifth Australian Open title ends in surprise fourth-round defeat.

Jan 24 1997 - Mannheim court sentences Peter Graf to three years and nine months, says he is guilty of evading $7.4 million in tax. Eckardt given jail sentence of two years and six months. Judge says no evidence that Steffi was involved in tax evasion and recommends investigations into her should be stopped.
